citation: L. D. Carr and S. B. McKagan. (2008). Graduate quantum mechanics reform. https://arxiv.org/abs/0806.2628
title: Graduate Quantum Mechanics Conceptual Survey (GQMCS)
description: A new essay-style conceptual assessment tool consisting of twenty-four questions, designed by the authors to test understanding of graduate-level quantum mechanics content such as postulates, density matrices, and entanglement. It was "given as an extra-credit pre-ﬁnal at the end of the second semester", with students given two hours outside class, and partial credit allowed. The survey was written before the first year and not consulted until after administration to avoid bias.
requirements: Administered as a post-test of material covered in the course; two hours outside of class for completion
constraints: Directed toward the authors' own concept of what is necessary for successful research, so it can be argued they taught to the test; not yet agreed upon by a larger number of researchers
target_learning_goals: conceptual understanding of graduate quantum mechanics, including postulates, density matrices, entanglement, scattering theory
examples: Used across all three years of the study; validated that students in the Sakurai-based benchmark course did not acquire understanding of periods III and IV
key_sources: L. D. Carr and S. B. McKagan. (2008). Graduate quantum mechanics reform. https://arxiv.org/abs/0806.2628
